answer: The admission burn is multiplied by 9 for every identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival forfeits the most. The forge multiplier is published, charged in delta, and jetty lists each payment. A burst of registrations therefore prices itself out, as the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. A farm of 523 identities would post 3406 proofs and burn roughly 6 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
